title: 'Spooktacular' BBC hit bringing huge live ghost show to Birmingham
excerpt: Uncanny Live: The Haunted Arena Tour comes to Birmingham’s Utilita Arena on October 29, 2027. Tickets for Danny Robins’ BBC show go on sale November 18.
content:
Ghosts are heading to Birmingham as hit BBC paranormal podcast and TV series Uncanny prepares to embark on its first-ever arena tour.

Uncanny Live: The Haunted Arena Tour will arrive at Utilita Arena Birmingham on October 29, 2027, as part of a major UK and Ireland run hosted by paranormal investigator and presenter Danny Robins.

The tour promises a night of ghost stories, unexplained encounters and audience participation, with Birmingham fans invited to decide whether they are Team Sceptic or Team Believer.

Tickets go on sale at 10am on November 18, 2026, through UncannyLive.com.

Robins will be joined by experts Dr Ciaran O'Keeffe and Evelyn Hollow, with the trio investigating extraordinary real-life paranormal cases that have not previously been heard or seen.

First-hand accounts and expert analysis will form part of the show, while members of the audience will also be able to ask questions and share their own ghost stories.

The Birmingham date is part of Uncanny's first arena tour, a major step up after two previous theatre tours.

Robins said: "I still pinch myself on a daily basis when I think about the way Uncanny has grown. This podcast that I started a few years ago, recording in my shed, is now hitting the road to play an arena tour.

"It's like the maddest, potentially paranormal, cheese dream!

"I've had a great time doing the last two Uncanny tours around the theatres of the UK, but making the leap to arenas allows me to deliver a show that's even more spooktacular and thrilling – expect something unlike anything you have seen before."

He added that audiences can expect a show that will make them "jump, laugh and question the very nature of the universe" while attempting to answer the ultimate paranormal question: do ghosts exist?

Uncanny launched in 2021 and has since grown from a BBC podcast into a wider paranormal franchise.

It was among the most listened-to shows on BBC Sounds in 2025 and has also made the jump to BBC Two.

Robins is also the writer behind hit West End play 2:22 – A Ghost Story, while his other paranormal projects include BBC podcast series The Battersea Poltergeist and The Witch Farm.

His previous Uncanny tours, I Know What I Saw and Fear of the Dark, played to sold-out audiences across the UK and Ireland.

The new tour begins at Aberdeen's P&J Live on October 22, 2027 before visiting Glasgow, Sheffield, Hull, Nottingham and Cardiff ahead of its Birmingham stop on October 29.

It then continues to Newcastle, Leeds, Manchester, Liverpool, London, Brighton and Belfast before ending at Dublin's 3Arena on November 12.

The show is suitable for people aged 10 and over.

Tickets for the Birmingham show go on sale at 10am on November 18.
